## TL;DR

Fixed the two restart-dialog dismissal defects from review round 1 and added regression coverage for Escape, overlay dismissal, and a saved dismissal across polling. The current branch also retains the requested unsupervised copy-command behavior and published-release gating from the original task. The required scoped RepoOS check passes.

## Work and rationale

The review identified two related state problems in `ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue`. First, the dialog’s close button persisted dismissal directly, but Radix also closes dialogs through Escape and outside interaction. Those routes emitted `update:open` and did not store the installed version, so a still-pending restart could cause the notice to return. Second, a status watcher could set the dialog root open based only on `restartPending`, even when the content was hidden because the current version had already been dismissed. That left the dialog root and rendered content out of sync, and repeated status polls could preserve that empty open state.

The branch now derives eligibility from restart pending state, matching the latest published version, no running release cut, and the stored dismissal value. The eligibility watcher controls the root open state, so a status refresh cannot reopen a dismissed notice. The root `update:open` handler writes the installed version when any close path emits `false`, covering the close button, Escape, and overlay interaction. The existing shot fixture continues to bypass local dismissal for predictable captures.

I added an overlay-dismissal regression alongside the existing Escape persistence and saved-dismissal polling tests. It asserts that closing through the overlay stores the installed version and removes the dialog. The test uses the overlay `pointerdown` event that Radix handles; a plain synthetic click does not invoke its outside-interaction path. Existing tests also exercise the unsupervised copy action and its confirmation, suppression while the release run is active, release-note scroll containment, and existing supervised behavior.

No production UI adjustment was needed for these findings because the implementation checkpoint already contained the state fix. This pass made the shared close behavior explicit in tests and verified the whole changed path.

## Approaches tried

I first reviewed the recorded round 1 report and traced the current component rather than repeating its code change. I searched the component and sibling UI code for other restart-open, dismissal, and close paths; the class was local to this dialog. I then added an overlay test using `.click()`. The test correctly failed because Radix’s outside dismissal is driven by `pointerdown`, not click. I checked existing dialog tests and changed the regression to dispatch a bubbling, cancelable `PointerEvent` on the overlay, matching those established tests. That test then passed along with the Escape and polling regressions.

I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The first run confirmed remote build, test, and browser-gate success but caught a formatter issue in the newly added test. I ran `bun run fmt` and repeated the required check against the formatted tree.

## Challenges and blockers

The only implementation-time surprise was the distinction between a browser click and Radix’s outside-interaction pointer event in the DOM test environment. The failure was isolated to the test simulation; once the test emitted the event Radix listens for, dismissal persisted and the dialog content closed as expected.

The successful final check ran on the remote validation runner because this repository uses its managed check pipeline. It passed the build, all 150 scoped tests across six test files, UI smoke, format, lint, CSS layering, theme and rendered contrast, hard-coded color, bare-require, branch artifact, and task asset checks. The report is this session’s handoff draft; RepoOS will finalize it against the checked tree.

## Key learnings

For Radix dialog behavior, persistence must sit on the controlled root’s `update:open` event, not only on a specific close button. That event provides one place for all close routes. Eligibility and open state should also remain a single flow: making the watcher follow the complete eligibility predicate avoids an open root with absent content after a dismissal.

When testing outside dismissal, use the event the dialog primitive actually handles. A `.click()` on the visual overlay is not equivalent to pointer interaction and can produce a false negative. Mirroring the existing overlay tests made the regression both realistic and stable.
